title: Should Prices End in .95 or a Round Number?

scenes.say: Nine ninety-five and ten dollars sound almost the same. Guests don't read them that way.
Shoppers read the first digit. In one catalog test, a dress sold a third more at thirty-nine dollars than at thirty-four.
But nine ninety-five isn't magic. It says bargain. A round ten says quality, and many restaurant managers price their best dishes that way.

props.caption: Myth or *fact*?
props.fact: It signals a deal. Round signals quality.

scenes.say: So: end grab-and-go items in ninety-five. Round off your signature dishes. And keep one style per menu section.
